business_summary: Provided investment advisory services and portfolios.
ai_claim: Claimed AI and machine learning used client data in investment decisions.
why_ai_washing: The SEC found that the advertised capabilities did not exist. This directly fits misrepresented AI use.
stock_market_connection: Private adviser; claims concern investing, not a listed issuer.
limitations: Settled without admitting or denying findings. This does not establish that every part of its service lacked AI.

business_summary: Offered portfolio analysis and investment advice.
ai_claim: Promoted expert AI-driven forecasts and claimed to be the first regulated AI financial adviser.
why_ai_washing: The SEC found those representations false or misleading, supporting a mismatch between AI positioning and delivered capabilities.
stock_market_connection: Private adviser serving investors.
limitations: Settled without admitting or denying findings; SEC registration is not approval of a product.

business_summary: Raised funds for an advisory business and managed client accounts.
ai_claim: Claimed an AI platform performed automated securities trading.
why_ai_washing: The SEC found the business was falsely described as having this platform. AI claims helped solicit investors and advisory clients.
stock_market_connection: Private fundraising plus trading in client securities accounts.
limitations: Entities and individuals settled without admitting or denying findings; other misconduct was also involved.

business_summary: Supplied voice-assisted drive-through ordering systems.
ai_claim: Claimed its AI removed human order-taking and reported misleading non-intervention rates.
why_ai_washing: The SEC found extensive human intervention and misleading disclosure of third-party technology. Automation claims overstated the product's independence.
stock_market_connection: Nasdaq-listed until September 2024; disclosure concerned public investors.
limitations: Settled without admitting or denying findings. Third-party technology and human support are legitimate when accurately disclosed.

business_summary: Operated advertising technology and promoted an AI fraud-detection tool.
ai_claim: Touted successful KAI tests and associated revenue in stock-offering materials.
why_ai_washing: Fabricated test reports and revenue misrepresented product efficacy and commercial validation. This combines AI capability inflation with accounting fraud.
stock_market_connection: IPO and secondary public offering in 2020.
limitations: The former CEO pleaded guilty; this does not establish culpability of every employee or prove that KAI never existed.

business_summary: Managed trades in clients' brokerage accounts under the WOLO Wealth name.
ai_claim: Claimed proprietary AI fully automated trading and eliminated downside risk.
why_ai_washing: The SEC alleges the purported software was not used for the described trades. If substantiated, this is misrepresented AI deployment coupled with impossible risk assurances.
stock_market_connection: Client brokerage accounts and options trading; not a listed company.
limitations: Complaint allegations, not a liability finding. WOLO was a business name, not an incorporated entity, according to the complaint.

business_summary: Offered a chatbot and tools for consumer legal tasks.
ai_claim: Promoted a robot lawyer able to substitute for professional legal expertise.
why_ai_washing: The FTC challenged claims unsupported by adequate evaluation. The pattern is overstated professional capability, even where AI is genuinely used.
stock_market_connection: Consumer service; no public-stock claim assessed.
limitations: A settlement is not a trial finding that every feature failed.

business_summary: Offered a shopping app for completing purchases across retail websites.
ai_claim: Presented checkout as autonomously completed by proprietary AI.
why_ai_washing: DOJ alleges human contractors secretly completed purchases while the automation rate was effectively zero. If proven, this fits concealed manual work and fictitious autonomy.
stock_market_connection: Private startup fundraising.
limitations: The cited indictment announcement is not a conviction or a check of the current docket.

business_summary: Sold facial-recognition software for security systems.
ai_claim: Claimed high accuracy, no gender or racial bias, and spoof resistance.
why_ai_washing: The FTC alleged insufficient support for broad efficacy and fairness claims. This fits unsupported AI performance assurances.
stock_market_connection: Security software; no public-stock claim assessed.
limitations: AI existence is not disputed here. The concern is how performance was represented.

business_summary: Sold an automated website accessibility tool.
ai_claim: Claimed the tool could make any website WCAG-compliant.
why_ai_washing: The FTC alleged misleading or unsupported compliance claims. The pattern is promoting an AI tool as sufficient for a broader outcome than demonstrated.
assessment: Strong documented concern: FTC final order
stock_market_connection: Business software; no public-stock claim assessed.
limitations: This does not imply that all automated accessibility assistance lacks value.

business_summary: Sold a tool for identifying AI-generated text.
ai_claim: Advertised 98% detection accuracy across content.
why_ai_washing: The FTC reported approximately 53% accuracy on general-purpose content. Extrapolating narrower performance to broader uses fits inflated AI accuracy.
assessment: Strong documented concern: FTC final order
stock_market_connection: Content software; no public-stock claim assessed.
limitations: The test result applies to the evaluated content and version, not all detectors or future versions.

business_summary: Sold screening systems to schools and other venues.
ai_claim: Promoted AI screening as detecting weapons while ignoring harmless items, with superior performance.
why_ai_washing: The FTC challenged efficacy claims. This fits overstated AI capability in a safety-sensitive product marketed by a public company.
stock_market_connection: Public-company product claims; not evidence of a particular stock-price effect.
limitations: The issue is performance claims, not proof that the system used no AI. Settlement terms do not establish every allegation.
sources: FTC case record: https://www.ftc.gov/legal-library/browse/cases-proceedings/evolv-technologies | Company-filed 2026 settlement notice: https://ir.evolvtechnology.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001805385-26-000040/noticeofpendencyandpropo.htm

business_summary: Operated an anonymous messaging app.
ai_claim: Claimed AI moderation would protect users from cyberbullying.
why_ai_washing: The FTC alleged that promised AI safeguards did not filter harmful messages as represented. This fits overstated AI safety assurances.
stock_market_connection: Consumer app; no public-stock claim assessed.
limitations: Other allegations concerned billing and children’s privacy; inclusion here is specifically about moderation claims.

business_summary: Marketed conversational AI services and business opportunities to entrepreneurs.
ai_claim: Promised business growth, substantial earnings, and refund protection.
why_ai_washing: The FTC challenged performance, profitability, and refund representations. AI branding supported outcomes that allegedly were not substantiated.
assessment: Conditional: FTC allegations and proposed order
stock_market_connection: Small-business purchases; not a stock offering.
limitations: This concerns misleading claims around AI, not a finding that AI was absent. The cited release describes a proposed court order.

business_summary: Sold services to establish and operate online storefronts.
ai_claim: Advertised AI tools for rapidly generating passive income.
why_ai_washing: The FTC alleged that promised earnings generally failed to materialize. The AI-washing pattern is an unsupported business outcome attributed to AI.
assessment: Conditional: FTC allegations and proposed order
stock_market_connection: Consumer business opportunities, not publicly traded securities.
limitations: Poor returns alone are not AI washing; inclusion rests on the alleged deceptive AI-linked earnings pitch. The cited announcement describes a proposed order.

business_summary: Sold managed online-store business opportunities.
ai_claim: Promised guaranteed income from storefronts using AI software.
why_ai_washing: The FTC challenged deceptive earnings guarantees tied to purported AI-powered stores. This fits unsupported AI-enabled profitability.
assessment: Conditional: FTC allegations and proposed order
stock_market_connection: Consumer business opportunities, not a stock-market investment product.
limitations: Treat both names as one case. The record does not by itself prove all underlying software lacked AI. The cited announcement describes a proposed order.

business_summary: Sold training and done-for-you online stores.
ai_claim: Marketed an AI-powered e-commerce business capable of substantial profits.
why_ai_washing: The FTC alleged that the promoted profits did not materialize. AI was used to support an allegedly deceptive opportunity pitch.
assessment: Strong documented concern: FTC settlement announcement
stock_market_connection: Consumer business opportunities.
limitations: Distinct from Automators’ former Empire Ecommerce brand. This is an earnings-claim case, not a finding that AI was absent.
sources: FTC settlement announcement: https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2025/05/ftc-action-ends-ecommerce-empire-builders-online-business-opportunity-scam | FTC original AI-related allegations: https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2024/09/ftc-announces-crackdown-deceptive-ai-claims-schemes

business_summary: Set up third-party online stores and sold business coaching.
ai_claim: Claimed AI could help ensure store profitability and high passive earnings.
why_ai_washing: The FTC challenged unfounded income and profit claims connected to AI. This fits overstated AI business benefits.
stock_market_connection: Consumer business opportunities.
limitations: Automators, Empire Ecommerce, and Onyx Distribution are grouped as one operation; not three cases.

business_summary: Sold managed storefronts to people seeking passive income.
ai_claim: Promised high passive earnings through a proprietary AI-powered system.
why_ai_washing: The FTC complaint expressly alleges false AI and affiliation claims. This supports both misrepresented technology and unsupported profit promises.
assessment: Conditional: FTC complaint and settlement announcement
stock_market_connection: Consumer business opportunities.
limitations: The case page describes an August proposed settlement. Do not equate that wording with adjudicated liability.

business_summary: Sold app-development services supported by software tools and human teams.
ai_claim: Marketed AI-assisted app creation as fast and simple.
why_ai_washing: Reporting based on former-employee interviews describes more manual delivery than the marketing suggested. This is a plausible overstatement-of-automation pattern.
stock_market_connection: Venture-backed private startup; not Microsoft’s own operating business.
limitations: Former CEO Manpreet Ratia denied misleading users and said the platform automated meaningful work. Earlier representatives described human-assisted AI. Reporting does not establish that no AI existed; insolvency is not proof.
